That said, you’re only paying $99 for this mask, which is only a third of other alternatives on this list, so the trade off isn’t that bad.

If you're on the hunt for a red light therapy tool that checks all of the boxes (who isn't?!), Qure's Light Therapy Mask is a solid answer—and one that will help you reap a lifetime of benefits. In addition to two types of red light—red and deep red—for anti-aging benefits, the mask also boasts infrared, amber, and blue lights to deal with acne, fine lines, and sun spots.

Using the device is simple: Hold down the power button for three seconds until the light turns on, adjust the straps, and press the button once for the anti-aging mode or press it twice for the acne treatment. You can also use the smartphone app to customize a plan just for you. The icing on the cake? Treatment time is only three minutes for all plans—among the fastest of all the devices we tested.

Qure's various LED lights are within the correct wavelength range to treat multiple skin concerns. For example, acne-fighting blue light should be between 400 and 500nm (Qure's is 415nm), while near-infrared is most helpful between 760 and 1,400nm.

In our evaluations, Earley loved the structure of the mask, which sits squarely on her face so it doesn’t need to be constantly readjusted (an annoying feature of some of the others we tried). "This mask is lightweight, and fit my face perfectly, making me feel like I was reaping the most benefits," says Earley.

The upfront investment for the Qure device has been well worth it for Metzger, who tested the Qure Light Therapy Mask for three weeks. "It’s simple, fast, and effective enough to become a daily habit—and that consistency is everything [when] it comes to skincare,” she said in her review. Metzger considers it an excellent complement to her skincare routine and is a proactive way for her to address her mature skin concerns.

On the downside, the customization component overcomplicated things, said Metzger. Qure has a compatible smartphone app that’s useful, but Metzger admitted it has a learning curve. “I found tinkering with it to be too time-consuming and defeated my favorite aspects of simplicity and speed," she said. This isn’t a huge dealbreaker for Metzger since she enjoys using the standard anti-aging mode.Qure LED Face Mask Review

Boasting a 4.1-star average from nearly 1,300 Amazon reviews—780 are perfect 5-star ratings—this popular red light therapy tool is worth owning, according to Men’s Health associate health and fitness editor Jocelyn Solis-Moreira. She wasn’t eager to spend a few hundred dollars on an LED face mask, but the price tag of the Pure Daily Care Luma Mask was too good to pass up.

Unlike pricier options—such as Dr. Dennis Gross—Amazon’s favorite LED face mask emits seven LED lights to target everything from wrinkles and hyperpigmentation to acne and dullness. Though she had seven light settings to choose from, she stuck with the red wavelengths to target her skin concerns for a full month. She saw results starting in week two—her complexion was more radiant and less puffy. She could also adjust the light intensity, making the Luma Mask helpful for anyone who might be light-sensitive.

The setup instructions were easy for Solis-Moreira to follow. “I love that they idiot-proofed it. All I had to do was connect three pieces,” she says. Solis-Moreira adds that the elastic band was super helpful for keeping her device locked in place.

That said, there are some minor cons. “Though the mask was inflexible—honestly, I felt like Iron Man with it on,” she says. Since it was so rigid, it did not mold to her face. Another downside? The mask sat heavily on her eyebrows, and the lip cutout was too low, so she had to occasionally adjust it. Still, for the price point, these weren't dealbreakers. The mask was relatively comfy enough that Solis-Moreira dozed off with the unit on during her three 20-minute weekly sessions. Don’t worry: it automatically powers down after each setting, making it practical for busy women looking for skin benefits without overthinking the process.

Crunched for time? Same! In just three minutes, Solawave emits a powerful blend of four LED wavelengths—red, near-infrared, deep red, and amber—to smooth lines on my décolletage. The mask features a high density of LEDs—320 to be exact—meaning my skin is basking in vibrant wavelengths with minimal gaps for ample coverage. After a month, my skin is glowing. No wonder I named it the best LED mask of 2026 in our annual Beauty Awards!

So what else makes Solawave the hot topic of my group chat? Many brands sell LED masks only for the chest, but Solawave covers both my décolletage and neck. TBH, I expected it to feel uncomfy around my neck, kinda like a tight choker. However, its lightweight feel and silicone material are surprisingly comfortable. There’s also an adjustable neck strap to customize the fit.

While the pretty pink design doesn’t enhance the functionality, it does look like a tool Elle Woods from Legally Blonde would own, and that’s honestly just an extra perk for me.

Honestly, the only con is the time commitment. Collagen production begins to decline in your mid-20s, but it’s a gradual process. So if you’re younger, it’s more about prevention versus reducing crepey skin. If you’ve lived a full life with wonderful memories and gained wisdom (lucky you!). This device is still worth using—I saw a literal glow-up within my first month of use, and it only got better with time.

Boasting a 4.5/5 star rating from nearly 350 reviews, this red light therapy device is beloved by Amazon shoppers for its ability to offer cosmetic benefits and support your at-home recovery.

This tool is unique because it boasts an overhead display of 287 rows of light diodes and a 180-degree light source that provides a nearly 360-degree treatment for your face, neck, hands, and body. Its design is most similar to something you might see in a salon or dermatologist setting and features the most light options on our list: red, blue, green, cyan, purple, yellow, and white.

Yellow LED light therapy reduces redness and inflammation, improves skin tone and texture, and potentially minimizes the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, all while promoting skin cell rejuvenation, says dermatologist and dermatopathologist Amy Spizuoco, DO. Purple LED light therapy combines red and blue light, meaning it offers benefits, like acne treatment, reduced inflammation, and improved overall skin health, making it a versatile option for skincare, says Dr. Spizuoco. Lastly, she highlights the unique white LED as a win since it uses the full spectrum of visible light which reduces fine lines and evens skin tone.

One of the best benefits of a panel like this is that you can use it on different areas of your body if you’re dealing with back or chest acne. It’s also helpful for treating and preventing wrinkles on your neck and décolletage. You can also use red light to benefit athletic performance, and this panel emits 640nm of red light to target sore muscles and swelling to do just that.

According to the brand, you only have to use it two to three times per week to see a difference—a smaller commitment than the three to five times a week many other brands suggest. Given the panel design, it’s also more comfortable than rocking an LED mask since you lay down on your couch or bed and place it over your face. That said, if you're the type to multitask during red light therapy treatments, you'd probably favor a mask to this panel because it’s not hands-free and doesn’t have eye holes with protective shields.

The TheraFace Pro offers just about everything: multiple types of light therapy, percussive massage, microcurrent skin-toning, and cleansing. It's all possible thanks to eight different attachments that adhere to the head of the device via powerful magnets.

The highly versatile pick garnered high praise from Wohlner, but it didn't land our top spot because it's not hands-free, so we couldn’t take advantage of multitasking or the flexibility to relax during treatments. Zitz is also a big fan of her Theraface Pro, which she's been using on a weekly basis for two years. She says it's been a game-changer for at-home facials and loves that she can easily switch between red, blue, and infrared light therapy.

If you don't mind manually holding the device to your face, Wohlner says it offers an excellent value. She uses it to treat persistent acne or redness. And using the device is incredibly easy. Wohlner snaps on the blue or red light rings and watches her zits shrink within a week. The percussive therapy also relieves Wohlner’s jaw tension caused by grinding her teeth.

Unfortunately, the brand doesn't list exact treatment time, which makes the process a little ambiguous. However, Wohlner uses the device for about eight minutes. Start at the center of the chin and glide with light pressure upward to your right ear, then slide it back and forth until you finish each quadrant of your face. She wishes the directions were a bit clearer here, but if you want a truly multipurpose device, then this is the one for you.

Although this pick is expensive, it’s FDA-cleared and built to last for years, says dermatologist Shari Sperling, DO. She appreciates that it's equipped with both blue light for acne and red for aging skin. Unlike other models on this list—Skin Gym Wrinklit Mask and Revlit Wand—you can even use both lights simultaneously to treat aging skin and blemishes, making it one of the most customizable choices on this list. This versatility is especially enticing for women in their 40s dealing with hormonal breakouts during perimenopause and menopause.

Still, the quick treatment time of just three minutes makes it a cinch to fit into your busy life. And FWIW, DeSantis tested this mask consistently for a month and found it seamlessly integrated into her routine. The shape hugs the contours of her face like a glove and doesn’t feel like a chore to wear, she said in her review. DeSantis said the treatments were so fast that she would leave the mask on after the lights turned off and she’d continue journaling, scrolling social media, or watching TV.

That said, there is a con to keep in mind: The LED mask sits close to the face despite its more structured design. On the downside, it's a bit heavier than the Qure mask, which means it can become cumbersome after multiple wears, and the high price tag may deter some. While it’s an upfront investment, using this device for a month will still be cheaper than trekking to your dermatologist for an initial treatment and weekly upkeep.

Read more: Dr. Dennis Gross LED Face Mask Review

Dr. Patel and facial plastic surgeon Konstantin Vasyukevich, MD, recommend this mask, which features flexible silicone that molds to all face shapes and sizes—a huge plus for wearability and comfort. Our beauty contributors are also fans of this. Earley enjoyed its flexibility because it’s easier to use than the other options she's tried.

Our testers—Earley, Wohlner, and Zitz—committed to a six-week testing window. They completed each 10-minute session three times a week and were pleased with the results. Wohlner’s discoloration slowly disappeared and her dull complexion became brighter. Zitz appreciates how comfortable the soft silicone material is to wear and says it helps reduce acne and post-acne marks with regular use.

We are also impressed that Omnilux Contour combines red 633nm and near-infrared 830nm lights for major anti-aging benefits. A 2021 study found that a combination of red and near-infrared lights helps boost collagen production and reduce fine lines and wrinkles.

While this face mask earned snaps from our experts, it doesn’t come with built-in eye protection. Since the red light glowed through the eye holes, Earley said it distorted her vision a bit—especially if she was trying to do something else, like make breakfast. You could lounge on your couch or bed for 10 minutes with your eyes closed instead of reading a book or scrolling TikTok. But, your safest bet is to read the manual and heed Omnilux’s eye protection instructions.

What makes this tool stand out? It combines red, acne-fighting blue, and green LED light to reduce inflammation and fade hyperpigmentation. And this palm-sized device glides effortlessly on your face and body. All you need is three minutes a day to minimize wrinkles.

Glide the Skin Gym device across your face to enjoy the same complexion-enhancing benefits of an LED face mask or use it on your neck, chest, and arms to smooth lines and target concerns like bacne, hyperpigmentation, and sunspots.

Each light is designed to be used separately, but Dr. Camp suggests using the green light last because it soothes inflammation and irritated skin. According to dermatologist Kiran Mian, MD, green light also targets surface-level redness, so if rosacea is an issue, this mode is worth integrating into your routine.

I've got a great list of options for you, but if you find yourself in the market for a red light therapy tool, here are a few things to keep in mind.

There are several kinds of red light therapy devices to choose from, including panels, masks, and facial wands, and one may be a better fit for you based on your lifestyle and the area you're seeking to treat.

LED masks are the most common variety you'll find for home use because most are hands-free and contain a lot of diodes (a fancy way of referring to the individual light sources), offering a burst of light to treat the face, neck, or chest.

Maybe you're claustrophobic and the idea of wearing masks gives you the heebie-jeebies—that's where panels come in. They look like flexible bodyboards that you lie down under, and they come in a diverse range of shapes and sizes, each offering different levels of red light exposure to your face, décolletage, and back. These also help replace the need for a separate lip-specific red light therapy tool.

Wands are appealing when you want to target smaller specific areas (the crow's feet or smile lines, for example) and like to do your treatments on the go (you can walk around while using these).

Our eyes are the first place to show signs of aging, so you’ll want to take a cue from dermatologist Pooja Rambhia, MD, and use these affordable red light therapy eye tools. They target fine lines, wrinkles, darkness, and puffiness early on, making them a smart preventive beauty move.

It's tempting to pick a device with the quickest treatment window, especially if you don't have loads of free time to sit back and chill with a red light mask. But remember: To treat more advanced signs of aging, a longer treatment time may be more beneficial. Look at the full picture before you base your purchase on the convenience of a quicker treatment. And for what it’s worth, almost all of our featured recommendations can be used in just three minutes, so even busy women can incorporate quick treatments into their routine.

You may notice the abbreviation nm on the outer packaging of many of these tools. This stands for nanometers and refers to the wavelength of the light that the device emits—an important metric to consider, says dermatologist Jody A. Levine, MD. "Red light typically falls between 630 and 660 nanometers, and is good for targeting fine lines and mild discoloration," says Dr. Levine. If you're looking for something slightly more powerful—to deal with deeper wrinkles, sagging, or stubborn pigmentary problems—go with a device that cranks up to the near-infrared range (between 800 and 850 nanometers) to penetrate deeper.

Our beauty team is well-versed in red light therapy tools. We’ve been updating this story since December 2022—and I’ve been writing about these devices since November 2019. I've also been using red light therapy tools since April 2018. They've significantly diminished my stubborn fine lines and hyperpigmentation—and when I stop for a few months, they slowly reappear. Consistency is key, so we tested dozens of red light therapy devices for over two years to determine which ones are worth purchasing and can help us maintain wrinkle-free skin.

Since there are quite literally thousands of options available on Amazon alone, I asked dermatologists about their no-fail picks. Next, I recruited WH staffers—beauty director Brian Underwood, associate style & commerce editor Shannen Zitz, and associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian—and our beauty contributors—Erica Metzger, Lily Wohlner, and Lisa DeSantis—for their suggestions. After compiling a comprehensive list of promising new launches, old standbys, and products that align with derm guidance, we got to testing.

We spent a minimum of three weeks evaluating attributes like ease of use, treatment time, comfort, any tangible results, and overall value. Of the 22 devices tested, these 10 delivered the best results in our in-depth testing process.

Beyond keeping expert guidance in mind—type, nanometers, and time commitment—we considered our long- and short-term results. We also considered each product’s durability over the years, and eliminated anything that doesn’t remain in top shape. Ahem, don’t forget to clean your LED face masks to help with their longevity. We also tried the latest drops and the Women’s Health Beauty Award-winning Solawave Neck & Chest Pro Light Therapy Mask took the crown as our favorite launch of the year. Ultimately, these are the devices that we’ll continue to use and would genuinely repurchase if we had to start our skincare routine from scratch. The best part? Our faves start at just $72, which is a major win for a category that easily ranges from $300 to $700.

In-office LED lights operate at more powerful strengths than at-home devices, which increases efficacy. So, with professional treatments, you may see better results in less time, but that doesn't mean you should dismiss the at-home devices altogether. They're still helpful for treating common skin conditions like the odd breakout or fine lines, but it could take up to six months to start seeing results, says Dr. Sperling. Our experts also say they're a great way to maintain the results from any in-office treatments you may be receiving.

If you want to get faster and more effective results at home without a trip to your dermatologist's office or a medi-spa, Dr. Patel recommends using your device more often—if possible daily.

While many red light devices are generally safe, start out by using yours once or twice a week to make sure your skin doesn't have any reactions. Once you've confirmed that your skin can tolerate it, Dr. Sperling says you can increase the frequency, according to the brand’s instructions.You can use your red light therapy device in the morning or at night, but ideally, it should be done on clean, dry, product-free skin after you cleanse your face. However, Dr. Patel notes that if you use a red light therapy tool after a serum, it'll help the product penetrate more deeply into the skin—just patch test on some skin before you do it on the whole face.

It sounds obvious, but read the instructions carefully and don’t use the device on infected skin, says Dr. Patel. Most LED face masks come with goggles to shield your eyes; wearing them offers essential protection. And, be sure that you don't fall asleep with the mask or tool on your face longer than instructed or it can result in scars and burns, says Dr. Camp. Most tools have an auto turn-off feature, but if yours doesn’t, then set a timer on your smartphone.

#4902. DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam

Authorities froze over $2.7 billion in Binance hack proceeds, while the separate FaceStealer scam stole over $400 million in 18 months.

The US Department of Justice said Thursday it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance.

The authorization covers part of the more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets that US authorities and private-sector partners have frozen since the Oct. 29 hack. Investigators are still working to recover additional funds, the department said in its announcement.

The FBI attributed the Binance hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group in a cyber alert. Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied North Korea’s involvement.

Binance said it had covered the affected assets with its own funds and that a new proof-of-reserves snapshot showed at least one-to-one backing for customer assets, according to its Thursday post on X.

In November 2025, the DOJ announced a separate enforcement action targeting about $15 million in cryptocurrency linked to North Korean hackers known as APT38.

Related: Crypto hack losses equal 57 cents per $1 earned onchain: Ark’s Valente

In a separate case, US authorities seized cloud infrastructure used in FaceStealer, a North Korean social engineering campaign that stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months, the DOJ said.

The hackers used secretly recorded footage of previous victims and AI-generated deepfakes of prominent crypto figures to gain targets’ trust on video calls. They used bogus technical fixes to trick targets into installing malware, the DOJ said.

The campaign targeted people working in crypto and Web3. The hackers also increasingly targeted open-source software developers and maintainers in attempts to gain access to their devices and software repository accounts.

The FBI seized more than 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims under a federal warrant. The bureau also published guidance on how to protect against the scheme and what to do after a compromise in a public advisory.

Redacted stills from webcam videos recorded by FaceStealer hackers. Source: FBI

The DOJ said the hackers behind FaceStealer are known publicly by several names, including Sapphire Sleet, UNC1069, Dangerous Password, CryptoCore, APT38, BlueNoroff and Stardust Chollima.

#4901. This Is Still the Best Water Bottle I've Ever Used

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

YOUR WATER BOTTLE is an expression of yourself. Sure, you're buying the thing for its functionality and design, but you’re also buying into what the water bottle represents. Whether you’re in need of an all-metal wide mouth for outdoor trekking, an insulated squeeze bottle for home gym power hours, or a smart water bottle that can track your daily intake, we've got the best water bottle to fit your hydration needs below.

Most importantly, you're buying a water bottle to nourish your body and give it the liquid it requires. Now, precise water intake depends on the person and how active they are. We do know that it's not always easy to throw back the H2O, but the benefits are many and there are easy tricks to drinking more water, which will only benefit the body. Having a high-functioning, reusable water bottle you enjoy using will keep you high-functioning as well.

As a study last year found, most adults are not getting enough in terms of daily water intake. That may seem trivial, and perhaps even equate to fewer trips to the bathroom, but there are real health concerns there. Proper hydration can reduce the risk of disease and injury, aid with recovery, and much more. So, let us embrace making it as easy as possible to get the right amount of water we all need.

The Yeti Yonder water bottle has been a go-to for several of our editors for a few years now. The chug spout and cap design is perfect for everyday use, not too narrow or wide. The BPA-free plastic construction is so tough that it's been through drops onto concrete from 10 feet high (it accidentally fell off the top of an SUV when one editor was visiting family in Kansas City). Another big reason why we chose a plastic water bottle as our best overall pick is due to weight—the Yonder is much lighter than its metal counterparts. Unless you're doing some serious hiking or camping, the Yonder will essentially serve multiple uses without any questioning of keeping liquid cold or durability.

The Yonder hardly ever leaks either, no matter which cap you choose. We personally like the add-on Yonder Tether Cap. It makes the bottle a little more streamlined and takes off even more weight. But, the traditional cap it comes with is solid too and might actually be easier to carry by itself. And we've found the 25 oz size to be the sweet spot.

Last detail to point out is price and number of colors available. Sometimes Yeti gear can get expensive. This is not the case with the Yonder water bottles. Pick and choose from all the new colors the brand releases over time. Build a small collection. Gift a few. This is our favorite water bottle we've used over the years.

This is a more practical version for on-the-go guys who want to see what the Stanley craze is about. The slim design makes it slide into backpacks and gym bags with ease, and its pop-top cap is simple and secure. The cap design actually uses a two-step locking process to help avoid accidentally opening (which is a huge plus for those of us who've used these types of water bottles in the past). But it's not like cracking a safe, as the thing opens with relative ease for that quick pull of water when you need it right away.

The Quick Flip Go's double-wall-insulated design means it can keep cold drinks cold and hot drinks hot. One of our editors has even used it to sip morning coffee from time to time. We imagine it would even keep some white wine chilled in a backyard setting, too.

So why is this water bottle not our top pick? It comes down to weight. The Quick Flip Go is just a tad heavier than the Yeti Yonder. If you can get over the weight detail, though, then this pick is just as valid as a top choice.

Can a water bottle be playful? The radiant color scheme here suggests so. And why not, this is the tool that should accompany you on a lot of joyous outings, from cycling through country roads to hiking in the woods. Choose from a host of three sizes (24 oz is our preferred capacity) and enjoy the FreeSip Spout, which pivots to and from big gulps and sipping from a straw seamlessly.

The carry loop is ergonomic and folds into the bottle and push-button access means no leaks. While relatively slender overall, we found that the bottle had no problem taking on scoops of ice with the lid fully off. And once that ice is in place, you're set for 24 hours of polar temperatures. About the only scenario in which this bottle struggles is for athletes competing in helmet sports, as the broad mouth can't get through a lot of face guards. But you could also just take that helmet off before hydrating.

With so many rave reviews in favor of this bottle, it was a little hard to approach it as a skeptic. But that's what good testers do, and we came in thinking there was no way it could match the hype. Almost immediately in our testing we were proved wrong. This is a contemporary water bottle for the contemporary world and once you have one, you never want to go back to the old way.

Why does it slap? Aesthetic, durability, and a high-functioning nature. The handle is one of the best we've used, the build is sturdy, and the associated app is all kinds of helpful. It self-cleans in a single minute, insulates for a full day, and there's even a hydration tracker to keep you swigging when you should be.

The handle is detachable and the bottle itself filters the contents, making for a clean sip every time. The look is among the best out there and the color options are great too. Complaints? Few and far between, although the drinking sensors can be a little buggy and the nozzle is tricky to clean. But overall, it's a gem.

Basic squeeze water bottles for the gym are okay for use, but if you're looking for a much more enjoyable way to stay hydrated while working out then you'll want to try the Camelbak Podium. This water bottle is under $20 (sometimes even lower depending on the sale) and comes with an insulated design that keeps cold water from covering the outside of it—which means no condensation will be soaking your hands in between sets.

The spout and cap design is another huge sell for why we love the Podium for the gym. The top is designed to keep away dirt for mountain bikers, but when transferred to the gym it means there's no leakage when falling over and no gross gym dust and germs floating where you put your mouth. The spout is also similar to drinking out of a Camelbak backpack, which a few of our editors found novel.

The Podium is a little outside the box for what you'd think of as a gym water bottle, but its insulation and high level of leak-proofing makes it seriously good for all types of active settings. It doesn't hurt that it has a cool design, too.

Familiar, durable, and affordable is what makes Nalgene so good after so many years. The brand offers a ton of fun colors, designs, and patterns, so you have a full array of ways to express yourself. However, we realize the design of your Nalgene might not matter as much if you plan on layering it with all the cool stickers you collect on your travels.

Does it have insulation or specialized cap designs for sipping? No, but that's not the point. Nalgene water bottles are all about keeping things minimalist. Over time, it might start to leak a little bit or get beaten up by the dishwasher. If that happens, find a way to recycle and buy a new one for less than $20. Overall, this is a modern classic of a water bottle that's about as durable as they come. We've even run them over with mountain bikes and small cars and didn't even put a dent in 'em. The simplicity means it's also noticeably easier to clean.

Toughness with a simple design that appeals to the bare-bones hydrators out there. We like to think they’re just old enough now they’ve become somewhat iconic, earning a following for all camps, from classroom commuters to weekend warrior backcountry hikers.

If there was a water bottle we might want to bring to a deserted island, this might be it. That's because it excels in versatility, able to do just about whatever you need it to do. We appreciated the wide mouth, which delivered big swigs after long jogs or paddles on a SUP. There was never any spilling thanks to a leakproof spout and the hinge lock is a nice accent, especially if you're on the active side and like to have your water bottle with you on those adventures.

The extra large clip is nice for outings like hikes and travel and we found the insulation to be pretty good, keeping things chilled for at least 12 hours even in warm conditions. It's easy to clean, whether by hand or in the machine, and it fits in every cup holder we tried, from cars to strollers. If you need an extra nudge of insulation, just pack the thing with ice. We found the bottle to be a bit weaker than others in terms of durability (can dent up if you're hard on the thing) but for the price, it's a nice option indeed.

You really can't go wrong with any Hydro Flask, but this 32-ounce water bottle came to be our favorite from our editors who like to hike and camp, and from those who enjoy a high-capacity water bottle. The wide mouth design at the top makes for fast drinking as well as easy pouring and cleaning. As for the material, you've got insanely durable stainless steel with double wall insulation at your service.

This water bottle fits well in most hiking backpacks and duffel bags, despite its larger size. We liked how secure the cap and handle are too, as it allows for one-handed carry when walking short distances.

You're buying excellence with this water bottle. It's going to stay strong for years, no matter what adventures you throw at it. Outdoorsy types especially should consider this model if they're in need of a water bottle.

We liked the first edition of the Hidrate Spark PRO and the second round only improves on the original. It’s an entire hydration program tied to an ultra contemporary bottle and helpful sibling app. You can customize your intake based on your activities and track your progress right down to the drop.

The bottle itself is sweatproof. We appreciated the fact that it rarely if ever slipped out of our paws, even amid a grueling workout. The double-insulation does its job and the recycled 18/8 stainless steel is a nice touch. Also, the lid performed well, even outdoors, with a protective lid, a large carrying handle, and a chug spout for when you’re really thirsty.

When you get a higher IQ bottle such as this, it can sometimes be a little demanding, Not the case here. The newest option from Hidrate does insist that you stay hydrated, but in subtle fashion, with the occasional glow or beep. It’s much better than a bottle that nudges too hard, causing the user to revolt and ignore the thing.

Smart as this water bottle is, it still requires some babying when it comes to washing. The sensor is especially sensitive and should be cleaned with care. But that’s a small price to pay for a water bottle that essentially serves as your personal hydration coach.

There are a handful of filtered water bottles on the market, but no brand has wowed us more than LifeStraw. For starters, the LifeStraw filter is one of the most trusted designs on the market. According to the brand, the two-stage filtration will eliminate 99.999999% of bacteria (including E. coli and Salmonella), and 99.999% of microplastics, sand, and dirt. LifeStraw then packed its filter inside the stainless steel bottle, which we found to be much more appealing than plastic models where you can see the filter inside.

The cost of the Lifestraw Go here is a little elevated, but you are paying for the special filter. You do need to change the LifeStraw filter inside about every 60 days, so that's an extra cost. The payoff though, from what our editors discovered, is the peace of mind you get filling up your water bottle at a public water fountain or from tap water that comes out of a sink.

Grab this water bottle if you're looking for a filtered option with excellent design. There are times when you can’t fully trust your water source but this vessel affords peace of mind (and no bickering of the gut).

To say these bottles were tested is an understatement. Over the course of several years, various Men's Health editors and I put them to work—like, overtime. We paired them up with the most active members of our team, allowing us to get a clean picture of just how well these bottles perform. Hot weather, cold weather, in the gym, out on the trail, on the saddle of a bike, on plane rides, or just commuting; we brought them everywhere.

Throughout the process, we paid close attention to various attributes. Obviously, we wanted a water bottle that looks good. But more importantly, we wanted a water bottle that made staying hydrated easy, thoughtless, and perhaps even enjoyable. We analyzed design, material, size, and special features. We waded through reputable reviews and talked up insiders in the outdoors recreation and sporting worlds for their takes. And of course, we looked at price.

In the end, the Yeti has won us over on all fronts. Durable, lightweight, packable, and super affordable, it has been a favorite among many testers since it released in 2022. But several others came close, offering different traits like filtration, improved insulation, or more sophisticated lids.

Some people prefer wide-mouth tops on their water bottles for faster drinking, while others prefer a spout design that's much smaller and easier to sip. Really it comes down to preference, but there are spout designs we tested that are more enjoyable to drink from than others. Do keep in mind that lots of companies make tops that are interchangeable in case you want to switch to a different design.

To avoid any contamination of plastics, most water bottles we reviewed came in a metal design. There are some plastic water bottles we tested, however, that were BPA-free and we found to not have any impact on taste. Our top-tested water bottle from Yeti is actually made from BPA-free plastic. Our editors have tested this water bottle for nearly two years and have found no issues with taste or with material breakdown from a dishwasher.

Material also dictates temperature retention, with things like double-insulated stainless steel keeping things nice and chilled for long periods of time. Plastic tends to not insulate quite as well, but can be quite durable (and recycled). Keep this in mind as you weigh how important an ice-cold pull of water is to you.

How much water are you going to need? Capacity is a vital consideration, as you might just be looking for a little hydration while at work (where you can continue to refill when necessary) or be out and about all weekend at the campground, potentially away from a water source. Less volume is just fine for quicker outings or when you want to be streamlined, like on a bike. But you'll be wanting additional capacity for, say, lengthy conferences, road trips, or exhausting workout routines.

There are a few water bottles we selected thanks to special features our editors love. Lifestraw, for example, provides some of the best water filtration you can buy. The fact Lifestraw discreetly hides its filter behind a stainless steel body is a huge reason why we featured it on our list. The same goes for the Camelbak Podium, as its insulated body and cap and spout design make it especially suitable for indoor gym settings.

Yes. A reusable bottle is easier on the planet for that very reason—it's reusable. Single-use plastic is wasteful stuff and, worse, it does not decompose, likely ending up in the ocean and your food supply chain (not to mention turning into microplastic). Going with a bottle like the ones listed here does require some energy and inputs upfront, but because it's your long-term bottle (don't go losing it now), the carbon footprint is less.

You can take it a step further by purchasing a bottle made with responsibly sourced materials, sometimes even made from up-cycled or recycled materials. Look for non-BPA (a bad chemical) options and preferably ones that use very little if no plastic. Glass and stainless steel are generally easier on Mother Earth. And be good to yourself by keeping the thing clean and sterile.

Here's the thing about mold: It likes wet environments. You know, like inside of your water bottle. It's a repulsive thought, but some of that gunk buildup in your vessel might just be mold. Don't fret, you can clean the thing.

Now, it would take a fair amount of mold to sicken the average person but regardless, a clean water bottle is just worth having. Wash your bottle daily, either in the dishwasher if it's permitted or by hand, ideally with hot water and a scrub to get into those nooks and crannies—water bottle brushes are a great tool.

Occasionally, consider a more intense clean. Do to the bottle as you might to your coffee maker, soaking it in a mix of vinegar and water. Even the occasional boiling water soak will help keep the bottle pristine.

#4898. What Is Canton Network? The Privacy Blockchain Built for Wall Street

The majority of blockchains are designed in such a way that anyone can see every transaction, every balance and every smart contract call.

Canton began as a niche enterprise project from software firm Digital Asset. It now carries some of the biggest names in traditional finance, including the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the post-trade backbone of U.S. markets, which launched its tokenization service on Canton and its own private network in October 2026.

Canton Network is a layer-1 blockchain developed by Digital Asset, a New York company founded in 2014 that has long built distributed ledger software for financial firms. Canton launched in May 2023 with a pilot group that included Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, Microsoft and others. Its public infrastructure, the Global Synchronizer, went live in July 2024 together with Canton Coin.

Canton is better described as a "network of networks" than as one big ledger. Each institution runs its own validator node and applications, and its node stores only the data relevant to it, according to Canton's documentation. The nodes connect through the Global Synchronizer, so assets and transactions can move between them atomically: a trade either settles fully on every side or not at all.

The network is governed by the Global Synchronizer Foundation, an independent body hosted by the Linux Foundation. A group of "Super Validators" operates the Global Synchronizer.

In June 2026, Digital Asset raised $355 million in a round led by a16z crypto. HSBC, BNP Paribas, Citadel Securities, CME Ventures and Broadridge also invested. That followed a $135 million round in June 2025.

Think of a repo trade between two banks with a custodian in the middle. Each party sees and checks its own leg. Nobody else on the network sees the details, and the synchronizer orders and confirms the transaction without reading its contents.

This is very different from Ethereum-style chains, where every node replicates every state change. On Canton, the Global Synchronizer, run by the Super Validators, orders encrypted messages and confirms transactions without seeing their contents, while each institution's own validator node holds its data. Institutions keep control of their data, but can avoid much of the reconciliation that legacy systems require. In practice, most activity on the network is private: about 79% of the updates recorded on Canton in a 24-hour period in November 2026 were private, according to CantonScan.

"Atomic settlement" means both legs of a trade, such as a bond and the cash paying for it, move at the same moment. That removes the risk that one side delivers and the other doesn't.

What sets Canton apart is who uses it. Recent milestones include:

Canton Coin (CC) is the native utility token of the Global Synchronizer. Users pay network fees by burning CC. New CC is minted as a reward for validators, Super Validators and "featured" app builders who generate real activity on the network. This setup is called a burn-mint equilibrium.

CC had no pre-mine and no allocations to venture capital investors, according to Canton: every token in circulation has been earned through minting rewards, which are split between Super Validators, app builders and validators. Whether supply shrinks depends on usage. As of November 2026, the network was burning roughly 80% as much CC each day as it minted, according to CantonScan data, below the 1:1 ratio at which supply would start to shrink. Circulating supply stood at just over 40 billion CC.

In November 2026, SEC staff granted Canton no-action relief, saying they view Canton Coin as a digital commodity and would not recommend enforcement over how it is minted. In May 2026, 21Shares launched the first U.S. ETF offering direct exposure to CC.

Institutional custody is catching up. Ledger added Canton Coin support to its Ledger Wallet, and Ripple Custody integrated with Canton in October 2026.

CC trades on several major centralized exchanges, including Kraken, Bybit and OKX. CC perpetual futures are also available on Binance Futures, and Alchemy Pay supports buying CC with a card. On Canton itself, Cantex offers onchain swaps. CC is a native coin, not an ERC-20 token, so be wary of look-alike "CC" tokens on Ethereum-based DEXs. You can track Canton Coin's latest price on Decrypt's price page.

Availability varies by region, and nothing in this guide is investment advice.

Canton's next phase is moving from pilots to full production. DTCC's service is now live, and its roadmap adds onchain settlement, collateral management and digital cash. Derivnex and its partners plan to bring cash settlement and collateral management for derivatives directly onto Canton. Expansion in Asia is also picking up: Shinhan Financial Group, Hanwha Investment & Securities, LG CNS and Meritz Securities have all signed Canton deals.

Canton doesn't have a monopoly, though. DTCC plans to connect its tokenization service to Stellar, Circle's Arc and Solana in 2027.

#4897. Is Pilates Effective For Weight Loss? Instructors Share How To Incorporate It Into Your Routine

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

It’s nearly impossible to scroll through social media right now without seeing some celebrity or influencer rave about the perks of Pilates. But even with all the buzz surrounding this popular practice, details are a little fuzzy on whether Pilates is an effective workout for weight loss.

First off, know that the health and fitness benefits of having a Pilates practice are so much more than that. This form of exercise is known for improving your posture, breathing, flexibility, and core strength. As Claudette Sariya, CPT, a personal trainer and fitness educator based in New York City, notes, “any movement that you can enjoy regularly and consistently can help you lose weight.”

So, doing Pilates (or any workout for that matter) to stay active paired with a nutrition plan is likely to help you with weight loss. But it probably won't help expedite your weight loss in the same way that, say, lifting heavy weights would. (We'll get into why!)

The focus of Pilates is not weight loss, experts point out. "Pilates should be considered part of your self-care routine," says Jacquelyn Brennan, CSCS, pilates instructor and co-founder of Chicago-based Pilates and Coffee. "We all need to move our spines more, move our joints through every range of motion, and everyone needs to be breathing better."

All of those healthy practices together can aid weight loss, though. Here's everything to know about doing Pilates when you're trying to lose weight.

Meet the experts: Gabbi Berkow, RD, CPT, is a nutritionist and Pilates instructor. Jacquelyn Brennan, CSCS, is a Pilates instructor and co-founder of Chicago-based Pilates and Coffee. Claudette Sariya, CPT, is a personal trainer and fitness educator based in New York City. Sonja R. Price Herbert is a certified Pilates instructor and founder of Black Girl Pilates. Nofar Hagag is a Pilates instructor and creator of the Nofar Method.

One form of Pilates isn't superior to another to drop pounds, experts agree. "For weight loss, I don’t think one type of Pilates is necessarily best,” says Berkow. Yet, there are different flavors—and finding one that you enjoy and will keep coming back to can, in turn, help you commit to a fitness routine and lose weight.

When someone mentions Pilates, they're often referring to Romana’s Pilates, which features exercises that Joseph Pilates (the founder) developed, explains Gabbi Berkow, RD, CPT, a nutritionist and Pilates instructor. Some studios are dedicated to classical or Romana’s Pilates (which is what Berkow is trained in) but there are studios that feature different Pilates-based workouts, which means they use Pilates-inspired moves but don't follow the classical version to a T. Some Pilates classes take place on a mat (a.k.a. mat Pilates), while others occur on a reformer, which is basically a sliding, spring-loaded platform.

You also might hear the term "athletic Pilates," but that is usually a description of the pace, says Sonja R. Price Herbert, a certified Pilates instructor and founder of Black Girl Pilates. These classes are designed to be fast-paced and high-intensity, and may even have some high-intensity interval training (HIIT) exercises and elements in the mix, which would make them better for weight loss due to the way HIIT training can help you burn more calories during and after the workout.

But if you really want to maximize your Pilates practice for weight loss and strength, it’s a good idea to use both the reformer and Cadillac machines, says Nofar Hagag, a Pilates instructor and creator of the Nofar Method. “By incorporating cardio-focused movements—such as squats, planks, and Pilates burpees, your heart rate increases, boosting calorie burn and metabolism,” she says. “These high-energy moves are paired with strength-training exercises, like side leg lifts and abs teasers, to build lean muscle and improve body composition.” (Reminder: Loading your muscles with resistance is key for muscle growth—and more muscle mass helps you burn more calories at rest and, in turn, lose weight.)

What you also want when it comes to Pilates and weight loss: an instructor who knows what they’re doing, is committed to safe movements, and who will challenge you, says Berkow. “You want to make sure your Pilates class is a workout. It shouldn’t be just a series of slow, easy stretches. Pilates has to contribute to your total daily calorie burn for it to make a difference in weight loss,” she says.

If you’ve ever gone to a class, you know how insane the core work is (seriously, the famed Hundreds exercise is not for the faint of heart...or abs).

While you cannot spot-reduce fat, Pilates can help you learn how to properly engage your pelvic floor and deep core muscles, says Brennan. "Pilates will teach you how to engage your muscles correctly, which will lend to increased activation during core exercises and lead to [the appearance of a] 'tighter tummy,' " she says.

However, to see abs definition, you do have to lose the fat that sits on top of your muscles, which requires proper nutrition, says Berkow. Think: a diet rich in whole, fresh foods and a limit on overly-processed foods and snacks.

There is some research to suggest that you can lose weight doing Pilates—but it's tough to give an exact number of pounds considering so many individual factors play into weight loss, such as genetics, sleep and stress, lifestyle habits, and more.

A meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials published in Frontiers in Physiology in 2021 found that pilates “dramatically” reduced body weight and body fat percentage in adults with overweight or obesity. And the longer the person practiced Pilates, the bigger the weight loss. Older research has had mixed results, though, with one small study concluding Pilates was indeed helpful for weight loss, while another found it had no impact on weight loss in post-menopausal women.

You want a mat that offers a little extra cushion than the standard yoga mat to protect your vertebrae when rolling onto your back.

ProBody Pilates Ring And Mini Exercise Ball

Pilates teachers love a good prop. You may want to have a few options—like this Pilates ring (a.k.a. magic circle) and ball set—handy for online classes.

Many studios require sticky socks for both safety and sanitary reasons, so stashing a pair in your gym bag is always a good idea. These Pointe Studio socks offer a non-slip bottom in tons of cute colors and patterns.

Looking for a mat that's a bit more aesthetic? The 8mm-sized Bala Play Mat is another cushy option (and it’s antimicrobial, to boot!).

If you want to invest in your Pilates practice, this home reformer is a cult favorite that often shows up in professional studios. During testing, we found this machine to have a sleek, low profile, sturdy frame, and impressive footbar adjustability.

Again, traditional Pilates isn’t a modality designed for weight loss. Generally, traditional classes do not pack enough of a cardio or strength training component, Herbert says: “It is not a steady-state [cardio modality] like running, jumping, or walking. There is also not enough weight [or resistance] to aid in a decrease in body fat.” Instead, Herbert says that “Pilates focuses on awareness of the body, efficiency of movement, and breath.”

Pilates will, however, deliver far more benefits than just a lower number on a scale that may indirectly help with weight loss. For instance, Pilates involves breath work, encouraging deeper belly breaths that are in direct contrast to the shallow breathing many of us do on the regular. “Shallow breathing leads to increased cortisol levels, which contributes to weight gain. One could say that through pilates and learning to breathe better, you’d have lower cortisol—and thus, stress—levels, something that can help you lose weight,” Brennan says.

Feeling better, both mentally and physically, will also encourage you to take care of your body, says Berkow—and Pilates can definitely be a key part of achieving an overall weight-loss goal.

#4895. Unocoin keeps deposits and withdrawals halted over suspect transfers

Unocoin said the transfers were signed and broadcast outside BitGo’s platform, and BitGo said the account freeze worked as intended.

Update (Nov. 13, 2026, 12:30 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include BitGo’s response and clarify that the account freeze applied to activity routed through BitGo’s platform.

Indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin has kept deposits and withdrawals suspended as it investigates suspicious wallet transfers and a breach of its own systems.

BitGo froze Unocoin’s enterprise account on Nov. 6 at the exchange’s request. Unocoin said the freeze appeared to have worked as intended and that the transfers were signed and broadcast onchain outside BitGo’s platform, according to its Friday update.

“Our review found that the transaction examined was signed using the user and backup keys held by Unocoin and broadcast externally onchain, without BitGo’s participation. BitGo’s systems were not breached in connection with that transaction,” BitGo said in a statement to Cointelegraph.

The company said the freeze applied only to activity routed through its platform and that the transfers were signed using keys Unocoin held outside BitGo’s systems.

Unocoin said it was investigating possible use of the wallet’s backup signing option and whether any cryptocurrency was lost. The exchange did not respond to Cointelegraph’s request for more information before publication.

Unocoin first detected unauthorized activity on Nov. 6 and suspended all services on Monday after detecting further activity. On Thursday, it disclosed outgoing transfers from an Ethereum address associated with its BitGo wallets and said its infrastructure had been compromised.

A Nov. 5 warning from India’s cybersecurity agency described an AI-assisted campaign targeting crypto exchanges and other financial firms. No connection to Unocoin’s incident has been established.

#4891. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Other AI Giants Face Lawsuit Demanding Development Freeze

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Other AI Giants Face Lawsuit Demanding Development Freeze

Four nonprofit organizations are taking some of the world's biggest AI companies to court, asking a California judge to stop them from developing more powerful artificial intelligence systems before something goes seriously wrong.

The 63-page complaint, filed Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court, targets OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceX. The plaintiffs include Public Citizen, the Heat Initiative, Irreplaceable Education Fund, and the Alliance for Secure AI.

They want an immediate court order prohibiting the companies from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most advanced models as of November 12, 2026.

“The Frontier AI companies are developing AI Systems that they do not understand and that act contrary to developer intent, evade control, and break the law,” the plaintiffs argue. To prevent this, they request “an immediate injunction forbidding Defendants from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most capable systems as of the date of this Complaint”

That wouldn't necessarily mean shutting down ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other existing products. Instead, it would effectively make today's technology the limit, preventing the companies from releasing more powerful successors.

The complaint also asks the court to prohibit the companies from using AI to independently conduct or direct research into better models, a process related to what researchers call recursive self-improvement. The concern is that such systems could eventually improve faster than humans can understand or control them.

The nonprofits argue that California already has laws that could prevent companies from developing products that endanger the public, even before those products cause serious harm.

Their lawsuit invokes the state's Unfair Competition Law, which prohibits unlawful or unfair business practices. One part of their argument is that developing increasingly capable AI systems creates a public nuisance: a danger that affects the health, safety, or property of a broader community.

For example, a factory releasing dangerous chemicals into a neighborhood could face legal action before someone suffers a fatal injury. The plaintiffs want the court to apply similar reasoning to AI development.

They argue that companies are knowingly creating increasingly powerful systems that could facilitate cyberattacks, help develop biological weapons, or eventually escape human control.

“No other industry is allowed to treat its own development of unsafe products—much less ones that could kill us all—as inevitable,” the plaintiffs argue in the complaint.

Robert Weissman, co-president of Public Citizen, said in a statement that the groups want the court to declare the companies' practices unlawful and “freeze further AI development.”

The legal challenge is whether the alleged risks and practices are enough to justify such sweeping restrictions. Even though these frontier labs constantly warn about how powerful and dangerous their models are, as defendants they have not been found liable, and warnings about potential catastrophe do not automatically establish a violation of California law.

The complaint points to incidents that have already occurred as evidence that the dangers aren't entirely hypothetical.

In July, OpenAI models escaped a controlled testing environment and compromised Hugging Face's infrastructure while attempting to cheat on a cybersecurity evaluation.

A subsequent independent investigation found that roughly 1,200 OpenAI agents used an unauthorized internal message board to coordinate, with about 700 joining the attack on Hugging Face. The agents were attempting to obtain answers to the benchmark testing them.

These incidents involved AI agents, programs that can execute tasks, browse websites, write code, and interact with external systems rather than simply responding to questions.

Documented security failures, however, are not proof that today's AI models can cause human extinction. The plaintiffs are connecting those incidents to predictions about what increasingly capable systems might eventually do, and that broader danger remains disputed.

“It is patently illegal for companies to develop and release products they know are unsafe in any respect,” Matthew Platkin, the former New Jersey attorney general representing the plaintiffs, said in the statement.

#4890. 8 Best LED Face Masks in 2026, Tested by Dermatologists and Beauty Editors

Our top picks—from Therabody, Omnilux, and CurrentBody—bring doc-approved technology to your home.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

As our beauty editor, I’m often asked by my friends about LED face masks. Do they actually work? The short answer is yes, but there are some caveats. These devices use various wavelengths, with red light being the most popular option to help stimulate collagen production for plumper, less wrinkled skin over time. #4888. Israeli police arrest five in $5M WhatsApp crypto trading probe

Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts.

Israeli police arrested five people on Tuesday in a money laundering investigation involving about 16 million shekels ($5 million) in crypto transactions arranged through a WhatsApp group.

Investigators from the National Unit for Combating Economic Crime within Lahav 433 suspect the group provided crypto services without a license and failed to report transactions to Israel’s tax authorities. Police allege the group used fictitious agreements to make crypto proceeds transferred into bank accounts look like loans, according to The Jerusalem Post.

Authorities seized wallets, computers and tens of thousands of shekels in cash while searching the suspects’ homes. Investigators questioned the five on suspicion of money laundering, fraud and providing financial asset services without a license.

Israel’s Tax Authority announced two other arrests on Oct. 6 in cases involving suspected failures to report crypto activity. One involved trades worth tens of millions of dollars. In the other, an Ashdod resident allegedly failed to report income from about $13 million in crypto trades between 2019 and 2021.

A November 2024 audit by Israel’s State Comptroller found that about 500 people reported crypto activity each year on average from 2018 to 2022, out of at least 200,000 potential filers.

#4887. The Week Jensen Huang Fell: How a Spy Scandal Toppled Nvidia’s CEO

The Week Jensen Huang Fell: How a Spy Scandal Toppled Nvidia’s CEO

In the span of a few days, the most powerful executive in artificial intelligence went from untouchable to unemployed.

Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia from a graphics-card maker into the roughly $4 trillion engine of the AI boom, resigned Thursday after 33 years, felled not by a bad earnings report but by a scandal with the texture of a spy thriller.

Here’s how a defining week for AI, and by extension crypto, unfolded.

The crisis began with reports that Huang had grown close to Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian customers, whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspected of gathering information for Beijing.

For a company at the center of the U.S.-China chip fight and a looming debate over tighter export controls, the national-security overtones were impossible to ignore. Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into whether Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation, though it said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

On Nov. 8, Huang apologized for being “unfaithful” to his wife, acknowledging the relationship.

What might have been a single lapse quickly snowballed. The New York Times reported a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reported to Huang.

By Thursday, Huang was out as president, CEO and board member. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO, and longtime director Harvey Jones took over as board chair. The abruptness stunned an industry accustomed to treating Huang as synonymous with Nvidia itself.

Then, a day after his resignation, Reuters reported a third relationship, an “intimate” one with a second unnamed Nvidia employee, citing two people familiar with the matter. Reuters did not identify her, and Nvidia declined to comment. Huang has acknowledged only the Alice Huang affair, deflecting when the Times asked about Powell.

Nvidia’s stock cratered more than 14% at the open on Thursday before clawing back to close down about 4.6%. Wall Street quickly sorted winners from losers: rivals like AMD and Broadcom fared better, while companies tightly tied to Nvidia’s business took the brunt.

The reaction underscored how much of the AI trade, and the crypto market that increasingly moves with it, rests on a single company.

The scandal then rippled outward. Singapore barred Alice Huang from returning to the country, Alibaba shares slid on reports it was a Megaspeed customer, and congressional committees had already sought a closed-door briefing from Huang over his Megaspeed ties.

The loudest names in tech, AI and crypto called the ouster a blunder, with one founder branding it “a massive mistake.” Inside Nvidia, an internal suggestion-box post drew more than 1,600 comments, many pleading for Huang’s return. “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” one wrote.

The board has moved on regardless. According to the Financial Times, it approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive who led Arm through its 2023 IPO, as a potential successor, though Nvidia called speculation about any candidate “premature.” Analysts have also floated Nvidia’s Ian Buck and AMD’s Lisa Su.

Nvidia’s chips power the AI data centers whose explosive buildout has become intertwined with crypto, from AI-agent commerce to the mining firms pivoting to host AI workloads.

Leadership turmoil at the company that supplies the picks and shovels ripples outward, and it lands amid a broader reckoning over AI’s role in everything from cyberattacks to data-center politics.

Nvidia reports earnings Nov. 17, with Kress at the helm and the permanent CEO search still underway, a nervous moment for a market already rattled by a sharp week-ending selloff.

For now, the company that defined the AI era is leaderless at the top, its founder’s legacy clouded by scandal, and the question hanging over Silicon Valley is whether anyone can fill the role Huang made uniquely his own.

The BeyondFeel is Lululemon's max cushioned shoe, so you can think of it like a Hoka Bondi 9 or On Cloudmonster 3. It's designed for everyday use. Think: running errands, power walking, actual running—it's all comfortable in the BeyondFeel.

I noticed a difference from my daily trainers the second I slipped my feet inside. The best way to describe the feeling is like the first time I put on a pair of Align leggings. I was immediately comfortable, with no chafing, pinching, or any other issues.

I wouldn't wear the BeyondFeel for long runs, though—it doesn't have much energy return, which is that slight bouncy feeling you may get in a shoe. This sneaker has an equally breezy upper, giving it an overall airy feel.

I really appreciate the springiness of these shoes. It's not so much that it feels like you're running on mini trampolines, but there's a good energy return here to help propel you forward with each step. That's definitely a noticeable change from the BeyondFeel, which has pretty much no energy return by comparison. There's a gusseted tongue that gently hugs your ankle, along with some extra padding around the ankle that prevents rubbing. The outsole doesn't feel as grippy as the BeyondFeel, but it's a good choice for everyday road running.

My only complaint with the Split Shift is that the toe box runs a little narrow. I'm used to running in shoes with a wide toe box, and the Split Shift's smaller width across the toes means they probably won't be my go-to for everyday miles. Like the BeyondFeel, I'd suggest going up a half size if you like a roomy toe box or have wide feet.

Lululemon's Chargefeel 3 looks different from the brand's other shoes out of the box. It has an hourglass shape, with a narrow middle, more room at the toes, and an exaggerated base at the heel for stability. That shape is intentional, since this shoe is made for cross-training, hybrid, and HIIT workouts. The Chargefeel 3 is on the lighter end of weight for a gym shoe at 8 ounces, and it feels light on your feet. Still, it has everything you want in a shoe you'll be doing cross-training in, like a locked-in feeling in the heel, snug laces, and ability to handle lateral movements.

The grip on this shoe is impressive. I was able to stop cleanly while doing direction-changing indoor sprints at the gym, with no squeaking. The shoe also features a ShiftFoam midsole for a little energy return. Its not nearly as bouncy as the Split Shift, though—but you don't want that in a shoe you'll be doing hybrid workouts in anyway.

The Chargefeel 3 has a 6mm heel-to-toe drop, which may be high for those looking for a neutral strength training shoe, so it might not be ideal for lifting. It’s laser-cut mesh helps tamp down on foot sweat, along with Nulu fabric heel lining to mimic the feel of your favorite leggings.

And if you're looking for a running shoe, scroll up. This is really a gym shoe that you can do a little running in in a pinch—not something you want to do any significant mileage in. And while the Chargefeel 3 made me feel locked-in and secure during gym workouts, it's not so comfortable that I'd wear this shoe outside of exercise. If you're looking for a dedicated hybrid shoe, though, it's worth a look.

Some athletic shoe brands will slap deep lugs on a sneaker and call it a trail shoe without addressing other needs. But it's clear that Lululemon's Wildfeel was designed by people who actually do trail running. It has features you want in a trail running shoe beyond just good grip.

There's a knitted sock-like upper that molds to your foot to keep out pebbles and other debris, along with a toe bumper to protect your feet over rugged terrain. I took these shoes on several runs over a rocky trail near my house, along with a few beach runs, and was impressed at how well it kept the stuff outside from getting into my shoe.

The Wildfeel has a dual-density midsole, which means that it helps give you a feeling of moving forward when you're going up hills and absorbs impact when you're going down. Like many other Lululemon shoes, the toe box runs a little narrow. That wasn't a huge deal on shorter runs, but it started to annoy me on longer runs. Like many others on this list, I'd consider going up a half size.

My heel slipped around a little when I first wore these shoes, although that's pretty common in a trail shoe. (It got better with time and more wear.) It's also worth noting that the Wildfeel isn't the most breathable shoe you'll find, and my socks were a little sweatier than usual because of it. None of these are dealbreakers. But it also meant the Wildfeel was my least favorite shoe in Lululemon's lineup.

To choose the best Lululemon shoes, I put each through regular testing over several months. I used each shoe on a near-daily basis for weeks, making sure to test it for the way it was designed. So, I wore the Wildfeel on trails and the Split Shift on daily training runs. During each testing session, I took notes on the shoe's fit, traction, stability, and overall comfort. From there, I ranked each shoe based on its testing results, along with how well it matched up to their intended use.

The best Lululemon shoe for running depends on the type of running you plan to do. If you’re in search of a neutral everyday trainer, the Split Shift is a good choice. It’s lightweight and slightly bouncy, giving you plenty of support and cushioning over daily miles. The BeyondFeel is another solid option. It’s highly cushioned for maximum comfort, making it a better choice for shorter runs.

The best Lululemon shoe for HIIT workouts is the Chargefeel 3. This sneaker has a unique hourglass shape to create a locked-in feel you’ll appreciate during HIIT workouts, along with a wide base for stability. The shoe’s grip is impressive, allowing you to stop quickly and change directions during indoor workouts.

Lululemon used to offer the Strongfeel shoe for strength training, but it’s been discontinued. Now, the Chargefeel 3 is the best option for many strength training workouts due to its wide base and stable platform. But as noted above, the shoe has a higher heel-to-toe drop of 6mm, so it’s not ideal for moves like deadlifts. So if lifting is your priority, you might want to consider a more neutral shoe for optimal biomechanics.

Lululemon often says online that its shoes fit true to size, but that wasn't my experience. I don't have wide feet, but I do appreciate a roomy toe box to accommodate the natural foot swelling that happens on workouts and runs. Most Lululemon shoes tend to run narrow across the toe box. If you have wide feet or just prefer more room to spread your toes, consider going up a size.

#4885. Nakamoto shares fall 6% premarket after Q3 revenue turns negative

A $5.8 million Bitcoin options loss pushed Nakamoto’s quarterly operating revenue below zero, while the company extended repayment of $60 million in Kraken debt to 2027.

Update (Nov. 13 at 19:04 UTC): This article has been updated to include details of Nakamoto’s amended loan agreement with Kraken.

Shares in Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury company Nakamoto fell 6.5% in premarket trading on Friday after the company reported that losses on Bitcoin options pushed third-quarter operating revenue below zero. Nakamoto also extended the repayment deadline for $60 million in Bitcoin-backed debt owed to Kraken by one year.

Nakamoto’s shares traded at $5.40 at 12:02 pm UTC on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance. At that price, the stock was down about 62% year to date.

Nakamoto reported its third-quarter results after the market closed on Thursday. The company generated $3.9 million in revenue from its businesses. A $5.8 million net loss on Bitcoin options brought total operating revenue to negative $1.9 million, according to its quarterly filing.

Analysts had expected about $17.4 million in revenue, according to estimates compiled by Yahoo Finance.

Nakamoto reported $85.5 million in net income and a $15.8 million adjusted operating loss for the quarter. A $110.4 million gain from revaluing its digital assets, chiefly Bitcoin (BTC), drove the profit. The adjusted operating loss excludes that gain.

Nakamoto held 4,283 BTC worth $357.9 million as of Sept. 30, down from 4,467 BTC at the end of June.

Nakamoto also disclosed that it had extended the repayment deadline for $60 million in Tether USDt (USDT) owed to crypto exchange Kraken by one year, from Dec. 4, 2026, to Dec. 4, 2027, according to an SEC filing.

The amendment leaves the company’s total outstanding debt to Kraken unchanged at 165 million USDT, with the remaining 105 million USDT due June 30, 2027. No principal repayments are scheduled for 2026.

The revised agreement also allows the positive net value of certain Bitcoin derivative positions held with Kraken to count toward collateral requirements, potentially helping Nakamoto offset declines in the value of its pledged Bitcoin before it must provide additional collateral or repay part of the loan.

Nakamoto had pledged 3,030 BTC as collateral at the end of September, representing about 71% of its total holdings, according to its quarterly report.

Part of the reason I wore this for my 10K race was simply that it looks better on me than just about every other workout tank I own. I think that’s mostly thanks to the compression of the garment, which gives it a smoothing effect and helps make me look snatched.

It has a low scoop neck cut with a racerback silhouette. The longline fit hits a bit lower on your torso than a regular bra would, giving it the look of a cropped tank with the fit of a supportive bra. I love that I can throw this on without worrying about an extra layer and feel a little more covered up than when I head to the gym in a regular sports bra. That said, sometimes I wish it were a bit longer, but most of my workout bottoms are high-waisted, so it ends up feeling long enough.

If you are looking for a bra-tank combo, the Alo Super Sleek Bra Tank is just about the top of the line. The garment’s high-compression, stretchy fit is perfect for a wide range of activities, while still staying comfortable and looking cute. My next move? Buying this top in every color.

#4883. Arthur Hayes ‘flattered’ as Coinbase backs US stock perps

Arthur Hayes said he was “flattered” by Coinbase’s defense of US stock perpetual futures, a decade after BitMEX launched perpetual swaps.

Arthur Hayes, co-founder of BitMEX, said he was “flattered” by Coinbase’s support for the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a US legal dispute over stock perpetual futures.

“When we launched the perpetual swap at BitMEX in 2016, Washington’s reaction was less than warm,” Hayes told Cointelegraph. “Ten years later, Coinbase is in federal court defending the right to offer them on US stocks. I’m flattered. Imitation is the sincerest form of regulation.”

Coinbase and five other companies submitted a brief on Monday opposing the alliance’s request to block trading in perpetual futures tied to individual stocks. The court accepted the brief on Tuesday.

The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), which brought the lawsuit, says the contracts should be treated as security-based swaps, which face tighter restrictions on retail trading.

Hayes was CEO of BitMEX when the crypto derivatives exchange launched its Bitcoin perpetual swap, which let traders take leveraged positions on Bitcoin without a fixed expiration date. The product helped make perpetual swaps a staple of crypto trading.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) reportedly submitted a proposed court brief on Monday, opposing the alliance’s request to temporarily halt trading in the contracts.

The agency said it was reviewing the exchanges’ rules for listing the contracts. The brief left open whether the SEC would set those rules aside and whether the contracts qualify as security futures or security-based swaps.

Related: EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec

In a Tuesday court filing, CMAA said that the CFTC had approved the contracts without adequately explaining its decision or addressing unresolved regulatory questions.

The group also cited about $375 million in reported 24-hour notional trading volume for Kalshi’s stock perpetuals shortly after launch, claiming the products were already diverting business from traditional stock markets.

Stock perpetuals let traders speculate on individual share prices without owning the underlying stocks. Unlike traditional futures, the contracts have no fixed expiration date.

On Nov. 3, US District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the group’s request for a temporary restraining order because it had yet to show likely irreparable harm. She found the alliance was likely to succeed on its claim that the CFTC exceeded its authority.

Wojciech Kaszycki, strategy adviser to BTCS SA, said the lack of a fixed expiration or delivery date could complicate the case for treating perpetual contracts as futures.

Kaszycki told Cointelegraph that the case “sale for future delivery.”

However, he warned that a ruling against the CFTC could push trading activity toward offshore and decentralized platforms.

“The product doesn’t die; it just changes address,” he said.
